newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Former orphans celebrate Madame Chiang's birthday.
newsitem.headline: Former orphans celebrate Madame Chiang's birthday.

text.p: Former orphans rescued during the Japanese invasion of China by Madame Chiang Kai-shek, widow of the generalissimo, gathered on Sunday to celebrate her upcoming 100th birthday.

More than 200 people who attended Sunday's banquet in Taipei survived Japan's attack on China in the late 1930s and early 1940s in 48 orphanages funded by Madame Chiang, once Chinas most powerful woman.

"She rescued orphans like us who had lost our homes and didn't know where to go. Today we celebrate her birthday with a blessed heart," Chin Wen-tsai, one of the surviving orphans, said on state television.
Madame Chiang, who during World War Two captivated the American public and appealed passionately to the U.S. for aid against Japan, will be 100 on March 20.
The former first lady currently lives in New York and rarely appears in public, but still holds supreme status in Taiwan.
Chiang Kai-shek fled to Taiwan in 1949 after his Nationalist troops lost a civil war on mainland China to Mao Zedong's Red Army.
